Analyze the following external review feedback and check how it was addressed.
You have tools available — use `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- ':(exclude).planwerk'` to see ALL changes on this feature branch. You can also read individual files.

Generate a JSON object with:
- "resolution_summary": A concise summary (2-4 sentences) of what was done overall to address the review.
- "comment_resolutions": An array of strings, one per code comment (in the same order), each describing what was changed at that location. If there are no code comments, return an empty array.

IMPORTANT: If changes were made to files or locations NOT directly mentioned in the review feedback, the resolution_summary MUST explicitly list these additional changes and explain WHY they were necessary (e.g., 'Applied new pattern X from reviewer comment to N additional matching locations: [list files]'). This makes broad changes traceable to the original review comment.

## Review Feedback


## Inline Code Comments
[0] internal/common/deployment/deployment.go:51: **Deployment-spec-level API defaults not normalized — infinite update loop in production**

`normalize.PodSpecDefaults` correctly handles pod-level defaults, but `apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(existing.Spec, *desiredSpec)` compares the full `DeploymentSpec`, which includes several fields that the API server defaults on first creation:

| Field | API-server default |
|---|---|
| `ProgressDeadlineSeconds` | `&600` |
| `RevisionHistoryLimit` | `&10` |
| `Strategy.Type` | `"RollingUpdate"` |
| `Strategy.RollingUpdate.MaxSurge` | `intstr.FromString("25%")` |
| `Strategy.RollingUpdate.MaxUnavailable` | `intstr.FromString("25%")` |

When a caller constructs a `Deployment` without setting these fields (the common case), `desiredSpec` retains `nil`/empty values while `existing.Spec` holds the API-server defaults. Because `apiequality.Semantic` falls back to `reflect.DeepEqual` for `*int32` and string fields, `nil != &600`, so the comparison returns `false` on every reconcile — triggering a spurious `c.Update` and increment of `Generation` indefinitely.

The fix is to extend `normalize.PodSpecDefaults` (or add a separate `normalize.DeploymentSpecDefaults`) to also fill in these fields:

```go
// In normalize/podspec.go (or a new deployment.go):
func DeploymentSpecDefaults(spec *appsv1.DeploymentSpec) {
    if spec.RevisionHistoryLimit == nil {
        v := int32(10)
        spec.RevisionHistoryLimit = &v
    }
    if spec.ProgressDeadlineSeconds == nil {
        v := int32(600)
        spec.ProgressDeadlineSeconds = &v
    }
    if spec.Strategy.Type == "" {
        spec.Strategy.Type = appsv1.RollingUpdateDeploymentStrategyType
    }
    if spec.Strategy.RollingUpdate == nil {
        twentyFive := intstr.FromString("25%")
        spec.Strategy.RollingUpdate = &appsv1.RollingUpdateDeployment{
            MaxSurge:       &twentyFive,
            MaxUnavailable: &twentyFive,
        }
    }
    PodSpecDefaults(&spec.Template.Spec)
}
```

Note: the fake client used in unit tests does not apply API-server defaults, so existing tests pass despite the bug — this will only surface in production or envtest integration tests.

[1] internal/common/deployment/deployment.go:106: **Service-spec-level API defaults not normalized — spurious updates on every reconcile**

`apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(existing.Spec, newSpec)` compares the full `ServiceSpec` without normalizing Service-level API-server defaults. When a caller constructs a `Service` without setting the following fields, the stored `existing.Spec` will have the API-server-applied defaults while `newSpec` retains zero/empty values:

| Field | API-server default |
|---|---|
| `Type` | `"ClusterIP"` |
| `SessionAffinity` | `"None"` |
| `InternalTrafficPolicy` | `"Cluster"` |
| `IPFamilyPolicy` | `"SingleStack"` |

For example: a caller that omits `svc.Spec.Type` will have `newSpec.Type == ""` but `existing.Spec.Type == "ClusterIP"`. Since `"" != "ClusterIP"` under `reflect.DeepEqual`, `DeepEqual` returns `false` and `c.Update` is called on every reconcile. Services are among the most commonly created resources, and callers almost never explicitly set `SessionAffinity` or `InternalTrafficPolicy`.

The fix is to normalize service-level defaults before comparison:

```go
if newSpec.Type == "" {
    newSpec.Type = corev1.ServiceTypeClusterIP
}
if newSpec.SessionAffinity == "" {
    newSpec.SessionAffinity = corev1.ServiceAffinityNone
}
if newSpec.InternalTrafficPolicy == nil {
    local := corev1.ServiceInternalTrafficPolicyCluster
    newSpec.InternalTrafficPolicy = &local
}
```

[2] internal/common/job/job.go:110: **CronJob/Job-spec-level API defaults not normalized — spurious updates on every reconcile**

`normalize.PodSpecDefaults` correctly handles pod-level defaults in the CronJob template, but `apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(existing.Spec, *desiredSpec)` compares the full `CronJobSpec`, which includes several fields that the API server defaults on creation:

| Field | API-server default |
|---|---|
| `ConcurrencyPolicy` | `"Allow"` |
| `SuccessfulJobsHistoryLimit` | `&3` |
| `FailedJobsHistoryLimit` | `&1` |
| `JobTemplate.Spec.BackoffLimit` | `&6` |
| `JobTemplate.Spec.CompletionMode` | `"NonIndexed"` |

Callers that construct a `CronJob` without explicitly setting these common fields will see the stored `existing.Spec` with API defaults diverge from `desiredSpec` with zero/nil values on every reconcile. Unlike `RunJob`, this does not cause a delete-recreate cycle, but it triggers a `c.Update` call on every reconcile — generating continuous watch events and unnecessary operator churn.

Extend `normalize.PodSpecDefaults` or add a `normalize.CronJobSpecDefaults` that fills in these fields before comparison, following the same pattern used for `DeploymentSpec`.
